question: The state of the network of structures for preventing and tackling violence against women is a danger to the women who have experienced violence as well as to its staff, since European funding is set to expire on 31 December 2025.

Significant blame lies with the current and previous governments, as for 14 years they have made the financing and operation of the network almost exclusively dependent on European programmes with expiry dates. EU and Member States guidance is part of the problem, not the solution. Directive (EU) 2024/1385 recommends the development of fee-based structures to protect abused women. In the light of the above: 1.

What is the Commission’s view on the permanent establishment of contract staff and the large-scale permanent recruitment of all kinds of specialised staff, and the creation and unhindered operation of free state structures to prevent and respond to violence against women, without the involvement of NGOs and private actors?

What is the Commission’s view on the fact that the structures’ functioning is defined by the ‘cost-benefit’ policy, as evidenced by Directive (EU) 2024/1385, which is completely at odds with the real needs of abused women for protection?

What is the Commission’s view on the fact that, while it is provocatively calling for ordinary people to make sacrifices to fund huge amounts of military equipment, it is simultaneously – in the name of budgetary discipline – cutting funding and creating dangerous avenues for the commercialisation of the network of structures to prevent and tackle violence against women?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.2.2026) The Directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence1 aims to ensure that all victims of violence against women and domestic violence across Europe can benefit from the same comprehensive set of strong measures of prevention, protection, support, access to justice and improved coordination and cooperation.

In this regard, Article 25 of the Directive obliges Member States to ensure that specialist support services are available for victims and Member States are obliged to ensure that sufficient human and financial resources are available to provide these specialist support services.

Recital 58 of the Directive further clarifies that specialist support could be provided by public authorities, victims’ support organisations, or other non-governmental organisations, taking into account the geography and demographic composition of the Member States.

In addition, Member States are obliged to cooperate and hold regular consultations with civil society organisations, including non-governmental organisations working with victims, concerning the provision of adequate support to victims. Member States, including Greece, will need to implement this Directive by June 2027.
During this period, the Commission is and will be holding implementation workshops to steer the timely and complete transposition of the Directive.
1 Directive (EU) 2024/1385 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 on combating
violence against women and domestic violence, OJ of 24.5.2024, L p. 1.
